subject: water anole
title: This Lizard Breathes From a Bubble on Its Head for 16 Minutes

scenes.text: This lizard jumps into a stream and doesn't come up.
It's a water anole from Costa Rica. Birds and snakes eat them, so they dive.
One was timed underwater for sixteen minutes. Lizards breathe air.
Look at its snout. A bubble swells and shrinks. It's breathing the same air again and again.
Scientists rubbed a lotion on some lizards so the bubble couldn't form.
Lizards that kept their bubble stayed under thirty-two percent longer. A scuba tank, built from one breath.

description:
The water anole, a small lizard from the streams of Costa Rica, escapes predators by diving and staying under for up to 16 minutes.
It breathes out a bubble that clings to its head and breathes it back in, again and again. In a 2024 experiment published in Biology Letters, Lindsey Swierk of Binghamton University coated some lizards' skin so the bubble could not form; lizards with a normal bubble stayed underwater 32 percent longer.
How long can you hold your breath? Comment below.
first_comment: The researcher thinks they may last even longer than 16 minutes. Which animal has the best escape trick?
